title: Infinite Worlds World v2.4
description: Schema for Infinite Worlds story world JSON files. Single source of truth — schema_model.SCHEMA_SUMMARY is derived from this document at import time. IW-specific metadata uses x-iw-* extensions, which jsonschema validators ignore.

schemaVersion.description: Schema version this world conforms to. Read on every load, write on every save.

title.description: World title shown to authors and players.

background.description: Background lore and setting sent to the AI as context.

instructions.description: Main instructions sent to the AI on every turn.

authorStyle.description: Style guidance for prose generated by the AI.

firstInput.description: Hidden turn-0 prompt that seeds the opening of the story.

objective.description: Stated objective shown to the player.

mature.description: Marks the world as containing mature content.

nsfw.description: Marks the world as containing NSFW content. Requires mature: true.

contentWarnings.description: Content warnings shown to the player before starting.

descriptionRequest.description: Prompt used when the AI generates scene descriptions.

evaluationRequest.description: Prompt used when the AI evaluates player actions.

summaryRequest.description: Prompt used when the AI summarizes the story.

hideSkillSystem.description: When true, hides the world's skill values from the player UI.

showPawScriptButtons.description: Show PawScript-related UI buttons for this world.
showPawScriptButtons.x-iw-note: Semantics not officially documented; treated as type-checked passthrough.

imageStyle.description: Image style preset identifier. Null is tolerated but not recommended; prefer a string value.

imageStyleCharacterPre.description: Legacy: prefix text appended to character image prompts.

imageStyleCharacterPost.description: Legacy: suffix text appended to character image prompts.

imageStyleNonCharacterPre.description: Legacy: prefix text appended to non-character image prompts.

imageStyleNonCharacterPost.description: Legacy: suffix text appended to non-character image prompts.

illustrationStyleCharacterLowPriority.description: Low-priority illustration style hint for character images. Coexistence with legacy imageStyle* fields is an open question.

illustrationStyleCharacterHighPriority.description: High-priority illustration style hint for character images.

illustrationStyleNonCharacterLowPriority.description: Low-priority illustration style hint for non-character images.

illustrationStyleNonCharacterHighPriorit.description: High-priority illustration style hint for non-character images.

enableAISpecificInstructionBlocks.description: Enables AI-profile-specific gating on instruction blocks.

recommendedAIModel.description: Recommended AI model identifier. The fixture only shows null, but 'smilodon' is CONFIRMED valid as of 2026-08-06 — it round-tripped byte-identical through an import. The full enum is still unknown; the world editor's model dropdown should name it. Note that thinking variants are distinct strings ('smilodon' and 'smilodon-thinking' are not interchangeable, as selectedAIProfiles already documents).

charSelectText.description: Text shown on the character-selection screen.

designNotes.description: Author notes about the world's design. NOT sent to the AI.

skills.description: List of skill names available in this world.

autoAdvanceVersion.description: When true, the platform auto-increments version on save.

previewImage.description: URL of the preview image shown in the world list.

fullSizePreviewImage.description: URL of the full-size preview image.

fullSizePreviewImageOptions.description: Available full-size preview image URL options.

currentPreviewImageIndex.description: Index of the currently selected preview image.

allowChangeCharacterName.description: Allows the player to change their character's name.

allowChangeCharacterDescription.description: Allows the player to change their character's description.

allowChangeCharacterSkills.description: Allows the player to change their character's skill values.

allowChangeCharacterItemValues.description: Allows the player to change their character's initial tracked-item values.

allowChangeCharacterPortrait.description: Allows the player to change their character's portrait.

allowChangeCharacterNewPortrait.description: Allows the player to generate a new portrait at runtime.

conditions.description: Named-event registry (schema v2.4). Each string is a natural-language event the AI watches for; a `triggerOnEvent` condition is matched to an entry by exact text. Keep the two in sync.
conditions.x-iw-note: New in v2.4. Absent entirely in pre-v2.4 worlds. Exact-text keying is well-supported: the fixture's single entry matches its single triggerOnEvent `data` byte-for-byte, and no ID or index links them, so text is the only available key. CONFIRMED 2026-08-06: the registry is AUTHOR-MAINTAINED, not platform-derived. A round trip returned it byte-identical — still missing an event a triggerOnEvent used but had not declared, still holding a declared entry nothing used. The platform does not regenerate it, which also rules out regeneration as the mechanism enforcing the ten-event cap (a separate round trip kept all twelve entries, so the cap is not applied at import either). Keep `conditions` in sync with your triggerOnEvent strings. Tier 2 warns on drift in both directions, never errors, because a desync costs editor selectability rather than correctness.

permissionsOnceShared.description: Permissions granted to other users once this world is shared.

sharing.description: Other users can re-share this world.

editing.description: Other users can edit this world. Requires sharing: true.

victoryCondition.description: Optional victory condition for the world.

defeatCondition.description: Optional defeat condition for the world.

imagePromptDetails.description: Default image prompt details for the world.

NPCs.description: Non-player characters available in the world.

trackedItems.description: World state variables tracked across turns.

triggerEvents.description: Conditional events that fire when their conditions are met.

text.description: Message shown to the player when triggered.

alreadyFired.description: Platform runtime state — do not set in authored worlds.

imagePromptDetails.description: Structured image-prompt fields used by the platform's image generator.

illustrIsCharacter.description: Whether the subject is a character.

initialTrackedItemValue.description: Per-character override for a tracked item's initial value.

initialPCValue.description: Initial value for this tracked item on this character. A string is a single fixed starting value. An array of strings is a pick-one selection menu presented to the player at character selection: the player chooses exactly one option, and that single choice becomes the item's active value. The array is NOT a multi-value state holding every option at once, nor a [min, max, default] tuple. Trigger conditions (triggerOnTrackedItem) therefore evaluate against the one chosen value, not the whole option list.

initialValueBasedOnPC.x-iw-note: 'player' is structurally in the enum but is FATAL here: CONFIRMED 2026-08-06, IW DELETES a per-character initialTrackedItemValues entry scoped to 'player' on import, at any initialPCValue shape. A 2x2 isolated it to this field — array+'character' and string+'character' both survived, array+'player' and string+'player' were both deleted. Semantically consistent: 'player' means the value is not per-character, so a per-character override contradicts itself. The enum still lists it because the same field name on the tracked ITEM (trackedItems[].initialValueBasedOnPC) accepts 'player' happily — every such item round-tripped byte-identical in the same import. Use 'character' on the entry, or drop the entry and set the value on the item. Tier 2 errors on this.

description.description: Character description visible to the player.

skills.description: Map of skill name → numeric value. Keys must match world-level skills.

initialTrackedItemValues.description: Per-character initial values for tracked items.

positionInList.description: Ordering position in the NPC list.

detail.description: Detailed description sent to the AI.

location.description: NPC's typical location in the world.

secret_info.description: Information the NPC keeps secret from the player.

names.description: Alternative names the NPC may go by.

name.description: Display name (used for snake_case template variable).

positionInList.description: Ordering position in the tracked items list.

dataType.description: Storage data type. 'yaml' is the recommended structured format (schema v2.2) — enforceable via formatSchema. 'xml' is deprecated in favor of 'yaml' for structured data.
dataType.x-iw-note: A 'yaml' item may hold ANY valid YAML structure, to arbitrary depth — scalars, mappings, sequences, mappings nested in sequences, sequences nested in mappings, and block scalars ('|' literal, '>' folded). There is no flat-key restriction. See https://infiniteworlds.app/yaml-guide. PawScript walks nested paths with dots ($item.stats.friendliness).

visibility.x-iw-note: hidden_boring: AI cannot read the item (same readability as 'hidden'). Developer-confirmed, and import survival CONFIRMED 2026-08-06 by round trip — the value came back unchanged, clearing the [PENDING TEST] the KB carried as of May 2026. Source: iw_knowledge_base_v2_8.md.

description.description: Authoring description of what this variable represents.

updateInstructions.description: Instructions for how the AI should update this value.

autoUpdate.description: Whether the AI updates this variable automatically each turn.

variableName.description: snake_case identifier for this item (schema v2.2). PawScript references the item as $<variableName> (e.g. 'puppy_tracking' → $puppy_tracking). Should match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$.

enforceFormat.description: When true (schema v2.2), the platform enforces the item's value against formatSchema. Typically paired with dataType: 'yaml' and a non-empty formatSchema.

formatExample.description: Example value showing the intended shape of the item's value (schema v2.2), e.g. a sample YAML document. Empty when unused.

formatSchema.description: Pseudo-schema describing the item's structure (schema v2.2): lines of 'field: type' where type is 'text' or 'number', and a trailing '...:' line meaning 'more entries like this'. For a list-of-records value (the common case) the fields are prefixed with a leading '- ' YAML list marker, e.g. '- name: text'. Empty when unused.
formatSchema.x-iw-note: The pseudo-schema mirrors the value's own nesting: a field whose value is a sub-map is written as a bare 'field:' line with its children indented beneath it, and '...:' may appear at any level to mean 'more keys like these here'. It is not restricted to a flat list of leaf fields — see the puppy tracker in the canonical fixture, whose 'stats:' block nests 'friendliness' and 'energy'.

driftAcknowledgedForName.description: Platform-managed drift-acknowledgement marker (schema v2.2). The fixture only shows null; its non-null shape is an open question — type-checked passthrough only for now.

triggerEvent.description: Conditional event that fires when conditions are met

canTriggerMoreThanOnce.description: Whether the trigger can fire more than once.

triggerConditions.description: Conditions that must be true for the trigger to fire.

triggerEffects.description: Effects to apply when the trigger fires.

triggerCondition.description: Condition shape — lenient on `data` because polymorphic shape depends on `type`. The x-iw-condition-types registry below describes each type's data shape; Tier 2 validation enforces it.

data.description: Polymorphic payload whose shape depends on `type`. See x-iw-condition-types.

triggerOnCharacter.description: Fires only for specific player characters

triggerOnTrackedItem.description: Fires based on tracked item or skill value comparison
triggerOnTrackedItem.x-iw-note: not_equal: UI label 'is not exactly'; maps to JSON value 'not_equal'. Import survival CONFIRMED 2026-08-06 — it round-tripped byte-identical, clearing the [PENDING TEST] the KB carried as of May 2026. The same probe found the real hazard is elsewhere: a triggerOnTrackedItem whose `textComparison` is ABSENT or an EMPTY STRING has its entire condition deleted on import, whatever the inequality (fixture-proven `at_least` died for lacking the key). Always set textComparison. Source: iw_knowledge_base_v2_8.md.

triggerOnRandomChance.description: Fires with a random probability each turn

triggerOnTurn.description: Fires when current turn >= data value

triggerOnEvent.description: AI-evaluated: fires when AI judges the described event occurred
triggerOnEvent.x-iw-note: Schema v2.4: the event string should also appear in the world's top-level `conditions` array, which is what registers it in the editor's trigger UI. Tier 2 validation warns when it does not.

triggerPrereqs.data: {prereqs: string[] (trigger IDs that must have fired), firedThisTurn: boolean}
triggerPrereqs.x-iw-note: Shape changed in schema v2.4: `data` was a bare string[] of trigger IDs through v2.2 and is now an object wrapping that array as `prereqs`, plus `firedThisTurn`. The legacy bare-array form is still READ (older worlds carry it) and treated as prereqs, but CONFIRMED 2026-08-06: IW does NOT migrate it on import — it DELETES the condition, leaving triggerConditions empty and the trigger ungated, with no error in-game or in the export. Same-anchor object-form controls round-tripped byte-identical in that import. Tier 2 errors on a world declaring v2.4+ with this shape and warns below (so the v2.1/v2.2 back-compat fixtures still validate); migrate before importing either way. OPEN QUESTION: the fixture shows firedThisTurn only as false; true survived a round trip, so it is at least author-writable, but its runtime meaning is still untested — emit false unless an author has confirmed the other behaviour in-game.

triggerBlockers.data: {blockers: string[] (trigger IDs that must NOT have fired), firedThisTurn: boolean}
triggerBlockers.description: Blocked if any listed trigger has fired
triggerBlockers.x-iw-note: Shape changed in schema v2.4: `data` was a bare string[] of trigger IDs through v2.2 and is now an object wrapping that array as `blockers`, plus `firedThisTurn`. The legacy bare-array form is still READ and treated as blockers, but CONFIRMED 2026-08-06: IW does NOT migrate it on import — it DELETES the condition, leaving triggerConditions empty and the trigger unblocked, with no error in-game or in the export. Tier 2 errors on a world declaring v2.4+ with this shape and warns below (so the v2.1/v2.2 back-compat fixtures still validate); migrate before importing either way. OPEN QUESTION: the fixture shows firedThisTurn only as false; true survived a round trip, so it is at least author-writable, but its runtime meaning is still untested — emit false unless an author has confirmed the other behaviour in-game.

logic.description: Combinator — requires advancedLogic: true on the trigger

triggerEffect.description: Effect shape — lenient on `data` because polymorphic shape depends on `type`. The x-iw-effect-types registry below describes each type's data shape; Tier 2 validation enforces it.

data.description: Polymorphic payload whose shape depends on `type`. See x-iw-effect-types.

effectTellAIWhatToDo.description: Directive to the AI for next turn

effectGiveInfo.description: Append to secretInfo (not guaranteed to be followed)

effectChangeVictoryCondition.description: Replace victory condition (alreadyFired must be false)

effectChangeDefeatCondition.description: Replace defeat condition (alreadyFired must be false)

effectEndsGame.description: End the game. data: true allows the player to continue playing (victory-style); data: false ends with no continuation (defeat-style). Pre-v2.1 worlds used a separate canContinueEndedGame field; in v2.1 that semantic is consolidated into this data boolean.

effectModifyInstructionBlock.description: Modify an instruction block by ID

effectModifyKeywordBlock.description: Modify a lore book entry by ID (replaces both content and keywords)

effectSetTrackedItemValue.description: Set or modify a tracked item's value

effectModifyTrackedItemDetails.data: {trackedItemID, overrideName, overrideDescription, overrideUpdateInstructions, overrideVisibility, overrideAutoUpdate, name?, description?, updateInstructions?, visibility?, autoUpdate?}
effectModifyTrackedItemDetails.description: Modify tracked item metadata (not its value)

effectPresentChoice.data: {choices, message, updateMode, maxSelections, minSelections, selectionMode, valueDelimiter, targetTrackedItemId}
effectPresentChoice.description: Present player a choice; result saved to tracked item (blocking)

effectFireRandomTrigger.description: Fire a random trigger (selection pool/weighting unconfirmed). Historically absent from the schema but confirmed working in real worlds. Ignored (stripped) in Start-of-Game triggers.
effectFireRandomTrigger.x-iw-note: KB-empirical: confirmed working in non-SoG triggers. Source: iw_knowledge_base_v2_8.md 'Import Test Results'.

effectRunScript.description: Run a PawScript script (the string in `data`) when the trigger fires (schema v2.2). Scripts can ONLY mutate tracked items, referenced as $<variableName>; the natives $player and $game are read-only. Execution is transactional: any error rolls back all changes, is logged to World Debug, and the game continues. No unbounded loops. Docs: https://infiniteworlds.app/pawscript-script-guide and https://infiniteworlds.app/pawscript-reference
effectRunScript.x-iw-note: Nested YAML is reached by chaining dots: $item.stats.friendliness. A `for each` loop variable behaves the same way ($puppy.stats.friendliness += 1), so the depth of a YAML tracked item does not limit what a script can read or write.

selectedAIProfiles.description: AI profiles for which this block is active. Only relevant when enableAISpecificInstructionBlocks is true.

keywords.description: Keywords that activate this lore entry.

x-iw-template-variables.initial: initial_<varname> — initial value of any numerical variable
